subject: AP Statistics
title: Sample Statistics Walkthrough (Original Demo)
subtitle: 3 Original MCQs + 1 FRQ · Data Table & Desmos Calculator
mcqDirections: Original Demo Set: 3 self-authored AP Statistics questions to demonstrate summary tables and confidence interval items.
frqDirections: Original Demo FRQ: Summarize the statistical reasoning clearly in context.

questions.stemHtml:
A library tracks daily visitors over 5 days and records the counts below:

DayMonTueWedThuFri
Visitors4245444698
questions.promptHtml: Which summary statistic is least affected by Friday's unusually large visitor count?

questions.stemHtml: A quality engineer inspects batches where each independent item passes with probability $0.90$.
questions.promptHtml: What is the standard deviation of the number of passing items in a random batch of $n = 100$ items?

questions.stemHtml: A random sample yields a $95\%$ confidence interval for a population proportion $\hat{p}$ of $(0.52,\; 0.64)$.
questions.promptHtml: What are the point estimate $\hat{p}$ and margin of error $E$ of this interval?

explanations.1: The median ($45$) is resistant to extreme outliers, whereas the mean, standard deviation, and range all shift noticeably when an outlier ($98$) is present.
explanations.3: The midpoint is $\hat{p} = \frac{0.52 + 0.64}{2} = 0.58$ and the half-width is $E = 0.64 - 0.58 = 0.06$.

frqQuestions.stemHtml: Explain why random assignment in a controlled experiment supports cause-and-effect conclusions, whereas random sampling supports generalizing to a larger population.
frqQuestions.promptHtml: Write a brief two-part explanation distinguishing random assignment from random sampling.
frqQuestions.rubricHtml:
• Random Assignment: Balances lurking variables across treatment groups on average, supporting causal inference.
  • Random Sampling: Produces a representative sample from the target population, supporting population generalization.
